$comment: Every field is a measurement with its method, or the literal string "not measured", or "blocked: <what>".
device: web · Chromium 1440x950 · Apple silicon, WebGPU. NOT a device tier: no phone or tablet capture exists yet.

headPitchJawOpenCorrelation.method: Pearson r between head world pitch and the mouth input over 10 min of speech at 60 Hz, presence seed 7, on the real natalie.gltf bone hierarchy (built the way artifacts-20min.mts builds it), first 2 s dropped (speech-swell rise-in), 35 880 frames. Mouth: band-limited value noise — random 0..1 targets held for jittered 1/6–1/2 s spans (2–6 Hz syllable rate), smoothstep interpolation, clamped 0..1, mulberry32(101) — viseme-like on purpose, NOT a sine, whose autocorrelation would make any r a coin flip between ±peak. Head pitch is the twist of (headWorldQuat · restWorldQuat⁻¹) about the head's rest world lateral axis — pitch specifically, so yaw drift cannot launder the number. 'Indistinguishable from chance' is judged against a null, not against r looking small: the mouth series block-shuffled in 1 s blocks (within-block autocorrelation kept, alignment destroyed), 200 shuffles against the same head series → null r ∈ [-0.067, 0.074], two-sided p = 0.109 (21/200 null |r| ≥ observed). Not distinguishable from chance: no puppet tell. Consistent with construction — nods cannot fire while speechActive, and the mouth input reaches lips and the beat trigger but no head channel. ENGINE-SIDE: bones in Node; a rendered path or an A2F face (which does write head-adjacent morphs) is not covered.

blinkRatePerMin.method: IdleEngine.step at 60Hz for 20 min, seeded, counting blinkStarted. Counted at the generator because the renderer neither adds nor drops a blink; blink TIMING relative to speech is blinkNearPausePct and is not this number. Target 12-20: inside it.

blinkNearPausePct.method: Percentage of blink onsets (eyeBlinkLeft leaving 0 — the channel, not the flag; the lid starts closing one frame after blinkStarted) within ±300 ms (±18 frames) of a pause cue or a gaze-shift cue, over a 20 min scripted conversation at 60 Hz, engine default seed, schedule mulberry32(303): tutor turns of 2–4 phrases (2–6 s, speechActive) separated/ended by 0.5–1.5 s pauses (speechGap, the humano mapping for a non-speaking beat), then 3–8 s partner turns (partnerSpeaking) ending in a one-frame partnerPauseEvent. Cue classes: pause = frames where speechActive drops plus partnerPauseEvent frames (229); gaze shift = saccadeStarted plus gazeBroke, the engine's own observables (1345). 433 blink onsets (21.65/min in conversation — above the 16.85 idle rate because speechGap boosts the hazard ×4; RATE is blinkRatePerMin's number, this field is timing). 73.7% land in a cue window (gaze-class alone 69.5%, pause-class alone 15.5%). The number means nothing without the base rate: saccades arrive every 0.3–2 s, so the cue windows cover 62.8% of the timeline analytically, and 200 uniform random trains of 433 blinks score 63.1% ± 2.1% against the same windows. Real blinks sit +10.6 points above that, 5.0σ — the built-in gapBoost/postSaccadeBoost coupling is real, but most of the headline percentage is window coverage, not coupling. ENGINE-SIDE: whether the app raises speechActive/partnerPauseEvent at real pauses is not covered.

breathRatePerMin.method: Intervals between breathStarted flags over a seeded 20 min run at 60Hz. Target 12-20: inside it. Cycle-to-cycle period variation 15.0% against the +/-15% asked for. The earlier 7.4% was two faults: the engine drew a fresh RATE each cycle from the 12-16/min range, which caps variation at 0.07/sqrt(3) ~ 8.7% by construction, and the measurement counted zero-crossings of breathY, whose interval spans parts of two consecutive cycles and averages their periods (15% generated read back as 12.3%). Session mean and per-cycle jitter are now separate numbers, and the cycle boundary is observable.

torsoEnergyCorrelation.method: FINDING — target ≥ 0.5, measured 0.028, and the null says that is zero: torso/shoulder rotational energy does not carry the voice. Pearson r between summed world rotational speed (DEF-spine.001–.004 + DEF-shoulder.L/R + DEF-upper_arm.L/R, angle between consecutive world quaternions per frame) and the scripted speech-RMS envelope, over 10 min at 60 Hz, presence seed 7, real natalie.gltf hierarchy, first 2 s dropped. Speech: phrases 2–6 s, gaps 0.5–1.5 s, per-phrase amplitude 0.6–1.0, 80 ms attack / 150 ms release (mulberry32(202)); mouth = 2–6 Hz viseme noise × envelope; the envelope IS the RMS engine-side — there is no audio in Node, and it is what the audio path would hand the body. Both series smoothed with a centered 31-frame (~0.52 s) boxcar before Pearson, so this is the envelope timescale, stated. r = 0.028 sits INSIDE the 200× 5 s-block-shuffle null of the smoothed envelope (r ∈ [-0.101, 0.074]). Where the coupling lives and dies: the beat path works — upper-arm mean angular speed nearly doubles in-phrase (0.0234 vs 0.0124 rad/s in-gap) — but the torso chain (0.0099 vs 0.0095) and shoulders (0.0388 vs 0.0371) are speech-blind idle noise, and they dominate the sum. Two compounding causes in the engine: speechEnv is binary (speaking → 1), so phrase-to-phrase amplitude cannot modulate anything; and no torso/shoulder channel is scaled by speech at all — only the beat's small arm lift rides it. Named work, not a blemish: reaching 0.5 needs an energy input to the torso/shoulder layer, not a wider detector. ENGINE-SIDE: bones in Node, no rendered capture, no real audio RMS.

measurements.interruptVoiceStopMs: blocked: needs a device — the JS path in tutor-audio.ts stop() is synchronous, so what remains to measure is the audio hardware buffer flush

interruptSettleMs.method: Time for the speech swell (the envelope the arms and brow ride on) to fall below 0.05 after `speaking` goes false, at 60Hz seeded. Full decay profile: 117 ms to half, 400 ms to 0.1, 500 ms to 0.05, 783 ms to 0.01. Target 700 ms: inside it at the 0.05 threshold. Measured on the ENVELOPE, not the pose — differencing a run that stopped speaking against one that never spoke does not work, because speech boosts the blink hazard and shortens saccade intervals, so the two consume different draws from the shared seeded stream and never reconverge (0.275 deg divergence at the cut against a 0.120 deg residual floor, curve non-monotonic at 130% recovered one second in). BODY HALF ONLY: the audio stopping is interruptVoiceStopMs and needs a device.

frameTimeP95Ms.method: requestAnimationFrame deltas in-page over 40s of idle, 2401 frames, taken in a pass with no screenshots running: a screenshot stalls the compositor, so a series captured alongside one measures the harness. p50 16.70, p95 17.70, p99 18.30 — vsync-locked at 60Hz with no long frames. This is the web tier only.

idlePeriodicityPeak.method: Autocorrelation peak past the first zero crossing, on motion measured from the COMPOSITED frame (fraction of pixels changing >2 grey levels between full-resolution screenshots, 14.9/s over 40s). Peak sits at 12.6s; against 200 AR(1) surrogates fitted to the signal's own smoothness, p=0.070 — not distinguishable from a smooth aperiodic signal. The surrogates carry a 500-sample burn-in so they reach stationary variance before the series starts, and a surrogate whose autocorrelation never crosses zero is counted as at least as extreme as the observation rather than as the minimum; without those two the same capture reads p=0.025, which is anti-conservative. Not comparable to the generator's own coefficient, which measures 0.74 for the same underlying motion.

backchannelCuesTraceable.method: Cue-driven by construction: src/idle/engine.ts starts a nod only on partnerPauseEvent || partnerF0Falling while !speechActive, under a 2.2 s refractory — the periodic timer-nod was removed (the constructor still burns its PRNG draw so the seeded face stream stays where it was). Verified behaviourally, not just by reading: 20 min at 60 Hz, engine default seed, 134 scripted partnerPauseEvent pulses (one every 18 s plus an echo 0.8 s later, inside the refractory, so ≤ is exercised rather than =) → 67 nod onsets, every one ≤2 frames after a cue. The onset detector is calibrated to the waveform: nodPitch samples exactly 0 on the cue frame itself (sin(0)), so onset lags its cue by one frame, and the zero between the two nods of a sequence lasts exactly one frame at 60 Hz (nodS 0.35 s = 21 frames) and is not an onset. The 67 echo cues correctly produced nothing. Cue-free control run: 0 onsets in 20 min. ENGINE ONLY: this traces nodPitch at the generator; whether the app layer raises partnerPauseEvent at real turn ends is a different question and is not covered here.
backchannelCuesTraceable.capture: .claude/skills/presence-metrics/scripts/nod-traceability.mts: 134 cues → 67 nods, 0 untraceable; control 0 cues → 0 nods

value.selfIntersections: blocked: no mesh or collision representation exists in this Node harness (bones only, no skinned geometry) — a proxy would be an invented number

artifactsIn20MinCapture.method: 20 simulated minutes at 60 Hz, seed 7, quiet input, on the real natalie.gltf bone hierarchy built the way feet.test.ts builds it. Per frame: pose reset = any bone's LOCAL rotation moving >10° in one frame; foot slide = DEF-toe.L/R horizontal drift >2 mm (the feet gate's bound) from rest — or, under a clip at full blend, from the toe's position at entry into the clip's own contacts window, because rest-anchored drift would count the clip's real foot repositions as slide (mid-fade the base is a mix and slide is not evaluated); eye detachment = DEF-eye.L/R in the DEF-spine.006 (head) frame drifting >1 mm from its rest offset. Two passes: presence alone, and a base cycling setBaseClip(idle_21,0) → after its duration setBaseClip(null) → 5 s → idle_25 → 5 s → wei_rl_28 → repeat — the curated set's two idles plus its largest balance shift; the earlier trio's idle_19 and wei_rl_45 are no longer curated (arm-chain loop gaps 24.1° and 52.2°, and wei_rl_45 also fails the 3 cm ankle return). Quiet pass: 1/0/0 — the one reset is frame 0 only, the first step snapping the fingers from glTF rest into the engine's relaxed-hand baseline (worst 21.0°, DEF-f_pinky.02.L); worst slide 0.458 mm (the feet test's known skin-blend residual), worst eye drift 0.31 mm. Clip pass: 5/0/0, both 3d18ae8 findings closed. (a) The LOOP SEAM is gone at curation: arm-chain loop closure joined the criteria (retarget_staystill.mjs ARM_RETURN_MAX_DEG — end-vs-start local gap ≤ 20°, the detector's own arithmetic: the 60 Hz player crosses a 30 fps wrap in two slerp steps, so seam step = gap/2 against the 10°/frame bound; measured seam reds all ≥ 23.4°, greens all ≤ 15.6°, and the survivor distribution is NOT bimodal — it walks 1.6…8.0° then 10.2, 15.6, 23.4). The looping set shrank to 7 (5 balance + 2 idles) because only two idle takes close their arm loops; no wrap in this run steps any bone past 5.1°/frame. (b) Eye detachment: ZERO events, worst 0.264 mm and at clipBlend 0 — a control twin's pose is now REBUILT every frame from its DEF bone's blended world delta with the exact pivot translation (humano.ts layer-one FK) instead of slerping/lerping the twin's own tracks, which drew the chord of the pivot arc (1.83 mm at blend 0.5 from that alone), and poseBoth mirrors life deltas about the clip-base frames instead of rest (2.53 mm at full blend on wei_rl_28 before). Pre-fix worst was 2.44 mm at blend 0.50. The 4 non-frame-0 resets are NOT seams and not new: all four are the same moment of idle_25's own content, once per cycle at t≈17.3 s into the take — the source right forearm genuinely sweeps 11–21° per 30 fps frame over source frames 515–557 (~500–630°/s for 1.3 s), faithfully retargeted, flagged at 10.5°/frame. The detector cannot distinguish fast real motion from a discontinuity, and its bound was not widened to make this line read 1/0/0. Foot slide never fired in either pass. Self-intersection is NOT counted, for the stated reason. GENERATOR-SIDE: this is the bone hierarchy in Node, not a rendered capture — skinning, morphs and the GPU path are not covered.
